metrics.definition: verified output quality of a release candidate: first-pass closure, review findings, CI failures, retries and escaped defects, each over a declared cohort rather than a global average
metrics.unit: rates and medians over declared cohorts, with denominators
metrics.reason: MEAS-03 owns the definitions, denominators, cohorts and inclusion rules; this record holds the gate that requires them instead of restating them

metrics.definition: a task a client asked for is carried through to a verified result: its required gates, review and impact/documentation closure are met, and a cheap underbuilt attempt is not counted as success
metrics.unit: rate over comparable, risk-cohorted tasks with sample size and limitations
metrics.reason: the cross-platform golden end-to-end conformance laboratory owns the task-level evidence path; today's nearest tree evidence is the golden path this record requires

metrics.definition: supplied, retrieved, reopened, cited and expanded bytes/tokens per verified task, as observable proxies rather than a claim about internal model attention
metrics.unit: bytes and tokens per verified task, with the ledger's own accounting
metrics.reason: the context inspector and token ledger own the measurement; an uncited-context claim is not evidence and stays unknown

metrics.definition: precision and recall of graph-derived selection — affected tests, impact and drift — measured against what the repository actually changed
metrics.unit: precision and recall over the graph's own audit population
metrics.reason: the Specification Graph ↔ Implementation Graph completeness and drift audits own the population and the comparison

metrics.definition: a committed transition history replays from its own journal and the replay reproduces the published ledger record
metrics.unit: replayed entries against the published record; a mismatch is a failure rather than a partial pass

narrowing.scope: this measures the architecture evidence chain's own recovery, not a user-facing session, goal or mobile-client recovery

metrics.definition: queue, inference, tool, human-wait, review, CI and integration time separated rather than summed, with wall-clock lead time never treated as the additive sum of parallel task durations
metrics.unit: per-segment durations and rates with uncertainty
metrics.reason: Q14 owns the performance, scale, resource, latency and endurance budgets and their continuous benchmarks

metrics.definition: a client's control of running work from a mobile client: attention queue, approvals, intervention and parity of what may be done away from the desktop
metrics.unit: per-release capability coverage against the mobile architecture's parity contract
metrics.reason: MOB-04 implements mobile-first control; the architecture and parity contract it must satisfy are P02's (#399)

metrics.definition: the repository's own checks reach CI intact: every suite this repository's checks consist of and the rule driver run in the job, the depth the cap reads is fetched, and a failure reaches the job rather than leaving CI green
metrics.unit: the enforcement chain's own readings; a check that is dropped, moved, made non-fatal or swallowed is a failure

narrowing.scope: delivery latency and lead-time metrics are MEAS-03's; this measures delivery of the checks themselves

gates.permits: internal and invited design-partner previews that state in their own material that they are not production
gates.withholds: any quality, latency, compatibility or mobile-control claim

gates.permits: small external cohorts with the known gaps documented beside the build
gates.withholds: performance promises and any compatibility promise across releases

gates.permits: broad external use behind a documented support boundary
gates.withholds: production-support commitments and unmeasured platform claims

gates.permits: production use inside the scope the shipped release actually supports
gates.withholds: nothing this record states; the non-goals below remain outside every gate's claim

non_goals.does_not_support: mobile clients or mobile control of running work
non_goals.why: the cross-platform mobile architecture and parity contract are not locked and no client exists

non_goals.does_not_support: a marketplace or signed third-party extension distribution
non_goals.why: the signed extension SDK, permission review, marketplace and revocation model are not built

non_goals.does_not_support: performance, scale, resource, latency and endurance guarantees
non_goals.why: the budgets and their continuous benchmarks are not established

non_goals.does_not_support: compatibility promises across releases, including any stability level below 1.0
non_goals.why: the stability levels and what each promises are the licensing and trust policy's, and this workspace has not shipped a version

non_goals.does_not_support: cross-platform releases beyond the reference Linux environment
non_goals.why: the cross-platform golden conformance and release laboratory is not built

non_goals.does_not_support: automatic context, workflow or staffing optimisation and its rollback
non_goals.why: proposals for versioned optimisation exist as work, with no rollback surface in this tree

non_goals.does_not_support: providers or harnesses whose authentication or subscription entitlement is unknown or unlaced
non_goals.why: unknown entitlement is not permitted integration; it is a hard gate rather than an averaged score

golden_path.requires: every release candidate names the case and the committed trace that carries a client request to the evidence it publishes; a candidate whose evidence is not in this tree does not pass its gate
golden_path.reason: the cross-platform golden end-to-end conformance and release laboratory owns the full path; this record holds the requirement, the committed artifact and the case that reads it
